# dsh-image-scope
中文 · GitHub · Issues
A pixel ruler for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sidebar image preview. Hover to read the pixel under th
e pointer, drag one dashed rectangle to measure a region, and keep every measurement in true image p
ixels at any zoom level.
Built for development and design checks: compare screenshots, verify spacing, measure icon sizes, or
inspect a single pixel.
## Screenshot
A dashed selection from `(0,0)` to `(194,262)`, measured as **195 × 263 px** in the bottom-left bar.
The pointer is at `X 174 / Y 282`; the image is **512 × 512 px** and is being viewed at **183%**. M
easurements stay in image pixels at any zoom.
## Features
- **Hover coordinates** — the bottom-right bar shows X/Y, with a crosshair and a highlighted pixel c

ell.
- **One measuring rectangle** — drag to draw a dashed box; drag inside it to move, or use the e

ight handles to resize. Every edge snaps to the image bounds.
- **Readable measurements** — the bott

om-left bar shows the start pixel, end pixel, and `width × height` in whole image pixels.
- **Keyboa
rd** — Ctrl+D (⌘D on macOS) clears the box while the viewer has focus; Esc cancels a draw, move, or

resize in progress.
- **Zoom-aware** — Fit / 1:1 / − / + and Ctrl/⌘ + wheel (or trackpad pinch). Whe
el zoom is anchored at the pointer and toolbar zoom at the viewport center; coordinates and sizes st

ay in image pixels, not screen pixels.
- **Pixel-accurate rendering** — images switch to pixelated r

endering at 150% and above.
- **Keeps the built-in viewer** — the stock Image viewer is still availa

ble in the viewer dropdown.
- **Configurable** — colors, font sizes, box metrics, and overlay styles
live in `config.json`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Add `--profile <name>` if you are not on the default profile. You can also install it from **Plugins
→ Discover** once the marketplace entry is published.
## Usage

1. Open an image in the right sidebar (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO, or SVG).
2. Pick **Pixel Scop

e** in the viewer dropdown if it is not already selected. It is the default viewer for images.
3. Mo

ve the pointer over the image to read coordinates.
4. Drag to draw the dashed rectangle.
5. Drag ins
ide the rectangle to move it; drag a corner or edge handle to resize it. Edges snap to the image bou

ndaries.
6. Press Ctrl+D / ⌘D, click **Clear**, or draw a new box to replace it.
Coordinates are zero-based from the top-left pixel. Width and height count whole pixels, including b
oth ends, so a box from x=100 to x=199 is 100 px wide.
## Configuration
Edit `config.json` in the plugin package. The sections are:
| Section | What it controls |

| `font` | font families, font sizes, line heights |
| `canvas` | canvas background and text color,

scroll padding, focus ring |
| `selection` | dashed box stroke, width, dash pattern, fill, fill opac

ity |
| `crosshair` | hover crosshair color, opacity, width, dash |
| `pixel` | hovered pixel cell o

utline |
| `handle` | the eight resize handles: size, radius, fill, stroke |
| `selectionInfo` | bot

tom-left measurement bar: position, width, spacing, padding, colors |
| `hud` | bottom-right hint/si

ze bar: position, width, spacing, colors |
| `toolbar` | zoom toolbar and its buttons, value, separa

tor |
| `status` | loading and error text |
The Host reads the file on each page boot and injects it into the browser. After editing, refresh th
e page. A page that was already open before the plugin was first enabled uses an embedded default st
yle until it is refreshed; the injected file wins afterwards. If edits still do not apply after a re
fresh, restart DSH once so the Host half reloads.
## Compatibility
runtime dependencies, no install scripts.
The viewer uses the document-preview extension point and the `sidebar.right.tab.document` slot. If t
he built-in document preview is unavailable, the viewer is not mounted.
## Privacy
Everything runs locally. The plugin reads only its own `config.json` and the image bytes the preview
already provides; it does not send data anywhere and does not access credentials.
## Development
Plain JavaScript, no build step.
| Path | Purpose |

| `client.js` | browser viewer, config merge, generated stylesheet |
| `index.js` | Host half that i

njects `config.json` into the page |
| `config.json` | colors, sizes, boxes, overlay |
| `test/math-
test.mjs` | pixel mapping, snapping, hit-testing, move/resize tests |
